Three brand stories

Challenge, insight, approach, idea, channels and outcome, with my own role stated plainly in each.

Philips Personal Care

Men’s grooming and beauty · FleishmanHillard · 2025 to present

  • 2×category growth rate¹
  • +10 ptsGen Z brand love¹
  • 45–50%quick-commerce share¹
  • 54.57Mnreach, beauty, Jan–Aug 2026

Brand challenge

Grow faster than a male grooming market growing at 6.3%, win Gen Z, and do it with no TV: Philips runs 100% digital in India. On top of that, a steady run of launches had to land across hair styling and grooming.

Consumer insight

Gen Z follows people, not ads. The Yash partnership began when fans spotted him using OneBlade and asked Philips to collaborate. Quick commerce is search-led, so “brand building has to happen outside the platform”, as the Country Head puts it. And Indian hair has its own enemies: humidity, frizz, hard water.

Strategic approach

One brand, a different face per cohort: Ahaan Panday for OneBlade and younger buyers, Yash for all-in-one trimmers across generations, Rasha Thadani for hair styling. Creators and UGC take 20–25% of spend. A seasonal calendar pins each product to a moment: Mother’s Day, monsoon, Raksha Bandhan, wedding season.

Campaign idea

Toxic × Trimmers ka Baap, with Philips as sponsorship partner of the film and Beard Sense technology explained in the consumer’s language. “Designed for Indian Hair” for styling. OneBlade “Show, Don’t Tell” to let people try before they believe.

Execution channels

Creators and UGC, earned media, OOH, cinema (about 300 Toxic screens), Blinkit and quick-commerce takeovers, social, experiential.

Outcome

Philips Personal Health India is growing at twice its category’s rate, up 10 points in Gen Z brand love, with quick commerce at 45–50% share (from high single digits 18 months ago) and 15–20% of business.¹ Programme outputs from FleishmanHillard reporting: 103 coverages and 54.57Mn reach for beauty (Jan–Aug 2026); 63+ coverages on the ambassador announcement.

My role

Run the seasonal campaign calendar, research Philips’ high-end value proposition, hold brand consistency across touchpoints, and coordinate launches, ambassador amplification and spokesperson interviews (six in one cycle).

¹ Client-reported by Philips Personal Health India’s Country Head, BW Marketing World, Aug 2026. Category results belong to the brand; the programme outputs and my role are mine.

Lonnue Bodycare

Body care launch · Thrive body serum

  • Seedcreators first
  • Earneditorial next
  • Converton the brand’s own site

Brand challenge

A new body-care brand launching a new product, Thrive body serum, with no awareness and no proof behind it. The launch had to build awareness and credibility together.

Consumer insight

A serum is a product people want to see working before they trust it, and a new name has no equity to lean on. Borrowed credibility from creators and editors does what ads can’t.

Strategic approach

Stack trust in order: creators first for proof, editorial second for credibility, and the brand’s own website last as the home where interest converts.

Campaign idea

One launch narrative for Thrive, told in the same voice by creators, editors and the site.

Execution channels

Beauty creator product seeding, editorial media placements, and an exclusive launch on the brand’s own website.

Outcome

A complete launch system live across three channels: beauty creators seeded for proof, editorial coverage secured for credibility, and the brand’s own website as the launch home.

My role

Developed the launch narrative and sequenced the channels around it.

Royal Enfield

Motorcycles and cultural properties · 20:20 MSL · 2023–24

  • 1,050+avg exposures per campaign
  • 2launches: Bullet 350, Shotgun 650
  • 2cultural IPs: Motoverse, GT Cup

Brand challenge

Make launches and cultural properties feel like one brand, and reach beyond the motorcycle enthusiast who already follows Royal Enfield.

Consumer insight

Royal Enfield’s pull is cultural. Aspiration, community and music travel to lifestyle audiences who would never read a bike review.

Strategic approach

Treat launches and properties as one ecosystem: launches for reach, Motoverse and GT Cup for community depth, and luxury and lifestyle creators as the bridge outward.

Campaign idea

Motoverse, the annual music and lifestyle property, and GT Cup, built around riding culture. My proposal added luxury and lifestyle creators to connect the brand with aspirational communities.

Execution channels

Media and PR, creators, on-ground events, music and lifestyle content.

Outcome

1,050+ average exposures per campaign across the Bullet 350 and Shotgun 650 launches, and a 30–50% lift in brand talkability and lead growth across my 20:20 MSL portfolio.

My role

Co-managed Motoverse and GT Cup, coordinated brand, creative, PR and events teams on both launches, and proposed the lifestyle-creator extension.
